questions.q: What real-world event is celebrated annually as "Bitcoin Pizza Day"?
options: The first real-world Bitcoin transaction, in 2010, when 10,000 BTC was exchanged for two pizzas
The day Bitcoin's price first reached $1
The founding of Ethereum
The day the Bitcoin whitepaper was published
questions.explain: This 2010 transaction is genuinely considered the first real-world use of Bitcoin as currency, and crypto enthusiasts still celebrate it every year.

questions.q: Which country became the first to adopt Bitcoin as legal tender, and when?
options: El Salvador, in 2021
Japan, in 2009
The United States, in 2024
No country has ever done this
questions.explain: El Salvador adopted Bitcoin as legal tender on September 7, 2021, aiming to increase financial inclusion and reduce remittance fees.

questions.q: What actually happens during a Bitcoin "halving"?
options: The reward for mining a new block is cut in half, roughly every four years
The total number of Bitcoin in existence is cut in half
Transaction fees double
Bitcoin's price automatically drops by 50%
questions.explain: Halving reduces the new-coin mining reward — from 50 BTC at the genesis block down to 3.125 BTC after the fourth halving in 2024 — controlling inflation toward the 21 million coin cap.

questions.q: What did the SegWit upgrade in 2017 actually address?
options: Transaction malleability, while increasing how much data fits in a block
Bitcoin's total supply cap
The identity of Satoshi Nakamoto
The price of Bitcoin directly
questions.explain: Segregated Witness (SegWit) fixed a real technical issue with transaction malleability and increased effective block capacity.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does Chapter 4 pick up where Chapter 3 leaves off?
options: Ethereum, which builds on Bitcoin's blockchain concept but introduces smart contracts
A second, unrelated cryptocurrency with no connection to Bitcoin
A return to pre-Bitcoin precursors like Bit Gold
Nothing — Chapter 4 covers an entirely unrelated topic
questions.explain: Ethereum directly builds on Bitcoin's blockchain concept while adding smart contracts — the exact bridge Chapter 4 is built around.
